body: A man who said he slipped and fell on black ice in a Delaware shopping-center parking lot sued the center's owner, Cedar Christina Crossing, LLC, and Eastern LLC, the contractor it hired for snow removal, in Superior Court, alleging they negligently treated snow and ice in the lot. In his deposition he testified that he saw unplowed snow in the lot on the day he fell and saw a person plowing snow. The defendants offered maintenance records showing the lot had been treated earlier, weather data showing no precipitation after that treatment, and surveillance video showing the lot clear and dry with no snow removal under way when he fell, according to a law-firm summary published on JD Supra.

The Superior Court granted summary judgment for the defendants, and on March 23, 2026 a three-justice panel of the Delaware Supreme Court affirmed in an order written by Justice Griffiths. Applying Ridgeway v. Acme Markets, Inc., the court said that once the defendants showed reasonable care in addressing snow and ice, the burden shifted to the plaintiff, who offered only self-contradictory testimony that the video refuted and so raised no genuine issue of material fact.

For commercial landlords and their snow-removal vendors, the decision shows the weight Delaware courts give to objective records, such as video, treatment logs and weather data, when a plaintiff's account of conditions conflicts with them.
